context.label: Prison, death, and public memory

observations.body: Matthew recalls arrest, John’s challenge to Herod, fear of the crowd, a birthday oath, the requested head, burial, and the disciples’ report to Jesus.
observations.label: Herod’s oath ends in John’s beheading

observations.body: The passage presents Arresting, speaking, promising, killing, and burying as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Arresting, speaking, promising, killing, and burying

payload.posture: Read Matthew 14:1–12 as one movement in John the Baptist's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states matthew recalls arrest, John’s challenge to Herod, fear of the crowd, a birthday oath, the requested head, burial, and the disciples’ report to Jesus. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of John the Baptist's story.
payload.title: Herod’s oath ends in John’s beheading
